A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TimeRecipe research. Their main text, Figure 1, Tables 1–30, equations, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated between pages.

before.justification: v2 reports original forecasting experiments, analyses of module effectiveness and dataset properties, and architecture-selection evaluations in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including forecasting configuration rankings, statistical associations, and architecture-selection comparisons in the main text and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The canonical architecture, preprocessing and embedding options, feed-forward architectures, fusion strategies, and LightGBM architecture-selection procedure are unchanged. The added tuning description does not introduce a method component or revise the procedure.

E1.justification: LTSF, PEMS, M4, and the Time-MMD evaluation scenarios are retained. The new Time-MMD paragraph in Appendix B.1 describes the dataset already evaluated in Tables 3 and 5; it does not establish additional domain or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged. Tables 3 and 5 retain PatchTST as the existing-best comparator for Social_12_S and ETTh1_24_M, and DLinear for Environment_48_S and Security_12_S. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: No previously stated evaluation setting is revised, and no new evaluation is added. Appendix B.4 newly describes architectural tuning and fixed optimization settings for the existing experiments; this disclosure does not establish a protocol change.

E4.justification: The module-property analyses in Tables 2 and 4 and architecture-selection generalization evaluations in Tables 3 and 5 are unchanged. Appendix B.4 adds no tuning sensitivity experiment, ablation, or robustness result.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging results over four random seeds, t-tests for module-property associations, and a standard deviation and t-test for aggregate error reduction. No repeated-run information or statistical reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: Matched numerical entries, rankings, and reported findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 3 retains Social_12_S MSE values of 0.0854 for TimeRecipe Best and 0.0994 for PatchTST; Tables 6–30 retain the same ranked configurations.

T1.justification: The forecasting formulation, module equations, metric formulas, and six dataset-property algorithms are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs, and v3 adds no formal assumption, theorem, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: module-level benchmarking through over 10,000 experiments, configurations outperforming existing approaches, data-dependent module effectiveness, and a training-free architecture-selection toolkit.

C2.justification: Appendix B.4 newly argues that fixed optimization settings isolate architectural effects and architectural tuning balances expressiveness and training cost. Existing interpretations of dataset-property relationships and the substantive limitations in Appendix D are retained.

D1.justification: New Appendix B.4 identifies tuned architectural parameters, including hidden dimension, depth, and patch length, and describes mostly shared optimization settings. Appendix B.1 explicitly clarifies numerical-only Time-MMD evaluation. Exact settings and search ranges remain unspecified; hardware and resource links are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds seven cited works, including LSTPrompt, U-Cast, TAT, NAS-Bench-101, and NAS-Bench-Graph, through limited citation additions and the tuning discussion. The paper's positioning and novelty claim concerning module-level forecasting benchmarks remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds a hyperparameter-tuning subsection, expands the Time-MMD description, and adds corresponding cross-references. Dataset labels, acknowledgments, and publication headers receive limited edits; the main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 and all 30 tables retain their content and display structure. Algorithm blocks and appendix tables are repositioned through reflow, and the unchanged limitations discussion is consolidated instead of being interrupted by Tables 6–8.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves transparency through its new explanation of architectural tuning and optimization controls in Appendix B.4 and explicit numerical-only Time-MMD usage in Appendix B.1. These additions help readers interpret the existing comparisons. The benefit is limited because numerical hyperparameter settings and search ranges remain unspecified, while the empirical evidence and substantive limitations are unchanged.
